title: Skybridge Payments - POC scoping - workload modeling
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on workload characterization for two primary workloads (fraud scoring/embeddings and customer support chat). Discussed QPS/concurrency patterns, input/output token distributions, latency SLOs, and a benchmarking plan. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run capacity modeling and a 48h benchmark, Skybridge to provide sample payloads and success criteria, schedule follow-up to review results.
next_steps: Redwood: run workload capacity model and propose POC config by 2026-12-24
Skybridge: share 7 days of sample traffic & anonymized transcripts by 2026-12-23
SE to share preliminary cost estimate and POC onboarding doc
action_items: Alice Monroe: Send draft POC SOW and pricing and dedicated POC proposal (due 2026-12-24)
Ben Carter: Start capacity model and schedule benchmark runs (kickoff 2026-12-28)
Marco Diaz: Export and redact sample traffic (7 days) and share S3 link (due 2026-12-23)
Nina Chen: Provide network/VPC constraints and allowed egress IPs (due 2026-12-23)
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-12-22
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Alice Monroe (Redwood AE), Ben Carter (Redwood SE), Rajesh Kumar (Skybridge CTO), Lisa Park (Eng Mgr), Marco Diaz (ML Lead), Nina Chen (SRE)
Recording Link: https://redwood-recordings.example/ff-2026-12-22-skybridge (note: link placeholder)

[00:00] Alice Monroe: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, quick intros and then we'll jump into the workload details.
[00:18] Rajesh Kumar: Hi all, Rajesh here, CTO at Skybridge. We're evaluating Redwood for a short POC focused on two things: realtime fraud scoring / embeddings for risk signals, and a customer support assistant for web + mobile.
[00:30] Ben Carter: Great, Ben from Redwood infra team. Today we want to nail down success criteria, QPS patterns, token distributions, and agree on a benchmark plan.
[00:45] Lisa Park: Quick context: we have about 1.2M transactions/day, roughly 18k active sessions/day on the support app. System is multi-region in us-east/us-west.
[01:05] Marco Diaz: For the ML side the fraud scoring path is mostly embeddings + a small rerank/generative explanation. Support chat is the heavier generation workload.
[01:20] Ben Carter: Can you give ballpark QPS for each workload?
[01:27] Rajesh Kumar: Sure. Fraud embeddings: baseline is ~30 QPS average, peaks to 200 QPS during market open windows. Support chat: average 35 QPS, but spikes in incidents up to 300 QPS for ~10-15 minutes. Concurrency wise support chat typical concurrency 60-80 active sessions, peaks 350.
[01:50] Alice Monroe: Good — helps. Do you have token sizes for requests/responses?
[01:58] Marco Diaz: We profiled last month. For support chat input tokens: ~70% are short messages under 50 tokens, ~25% are 50-200 tokens (longer context/history), ~5% are >200 (multipart transcripts). Output tokens: median ~60 tokens for a reply, 95p ~220 tokens. For embeddings the input is usually 128-512 tokens depending on document chunking, output is embedding vector (handled separately).
[02:35] Ben Carter: So we should treat these as two separate POC workloads: 1) embeddings pipeline (throughput-oriented, lower latency for retrieval) and 2) chat generation (latency-sensitive, higher token output). Any hard latency SLOs?
[02:50] Rajesh Kumar: For support chat P95 we want < 400ms ideally, P99 < 800ms. For fraud scoring, we're okay with P95 < 1s but throughput is most important.
[03:05] Nina Chen: Also note we run strict egress controls; any hosted solution must support static IP allowlisting or private VPC peering. Data retention and audit logs are required — SOC2 is a must.
[03:20] Alice Monroe: Noted — Redwood has VPC options and can do Private deployment if needed; for the POC we can start hosted with VPC peering or dedicated capacity depending on results.
[03:33] Lisa Park: For the POC duration we were thinking 4 weeks with a small pilot then scale. Is that typical?
[03:40] Ben Carter: That's a good cadence. Our suggestion: 48-hour synthetic + sampled real-traffic benchmark, then a 2-week sustained run to validate production patterns. We'll capture tail latencies and cost metrics.
[03:55] Rajesh Kumar: What about concurrency and batching tradeoffs? We care about latency for the chat path. If you batch too aggressively we might break SLO.
[04:05] Ben Carter: Right — Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching with dynamic thresholds. For support chat we'll configure low-latency mode (smaller batch sizes) and KV caching for repeated context to reduce tokens. For embeddings, we'll run high throughput quantized model with bigger batches.
[04:22] Marco Diaz: Any model recommendations? We were considering a 13B/33B class for cost reasons, but open to 70B quantized if latency allows.
[04:32] Alice Monroe: For POC we typically test 2-3 model variants: a smaller 13/14B model tuned for latency, a 33B mid-tier, and a quantized 70B to evaluate quality/cost. We'll include throughput and token-cost per call in the bench.
[04:45] Rajesh Kumar: Sounds good. On traffic distribution: our internal logs show 60% of chat requests include a short conversation (<=3 messages), 30% are multi-turn (3-8 messages), 10% long support threads. Average input token per request ~45, but history expansion bumps that.
[05:05] Ben Carter: Helpful. For capacity modeling I'll ask a few more specific Qs: average tokens per second per QPS, average response tokens, and percentiles. Can you commit to the 7-day sample including timestamps and anonymized payload sizes?
[05:20] Marco Diaz: Yes we'll export and redact personal data. We'll include per-request token counts and timestamps.
[05:30] Alice Monroe: Great. For the bench plan we propose: 1) ingest 7-day traffic to create a replay profile; 2) run a 48h benchmark at real and 2x peak traffic; 3) collect P50/P95/P99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per million tokens, and model quality for a small eval set.
[05:50] Lisa Park: For quality check what do you measure? We need to ensure responses remain consistent and not hallucinate financial advice.
[06:00] Ben Carter: We'll run eval prompts (seeded) and compare model outputs across variants, plus check hallucination heuristics. We'll surface regression alerts in Redwood Console.
[06:14] Rajesh Kumar: And security — we need encryption in transit at minimum, plus KMS integration for keys if private deployment.
[06:24] Alice Monroe: Redwood supports TLS, per-customer KMS, and audit logs. For Private deployments we can integrate customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll include security docs with the SOW.
[06:39] Nina Chen: Also runbook for failover: if model or zone capacity drops, can we fallback to a smaller model or to a lower-cost region?
[06:48] Ben Carter: Yes our routing can fallback to another model variant or region automatically; we'll include a canary rollout and fallback policy in the POC config.
[07:00] Rajesh Kumar: Cost visibility is important — show token-level cost and per-route breakdowns.
[07:08] Alice Monroe: Redwood Console will provide token and latency breakdowns, and SE will deliver a cost projection against your observed traffic.
[07:18] (transition to more granular QPS/concurrency modeling)
[07:25] Ben Carter: Let's write down the numbers we heard: embeddings workload average 30 QPS, peak 200 QPS; support chat average 35 QPS, peak 300 QPS with 10-15 minute bursts, concurrency typical 60-80, peak 350. Any other seasonal patterns?
[07:45] Rajesh Kumar: Weekday peaks align with business hours, we also have monthly batch jobs that create spikes for embeddings between 02:00-03:00 UTC (about 400 QPS for ~30 minutes).
[08:00] Marco Diaz: Latency tolerance for the batch embedding window is looser but the volume is high.
[08:08] Ben Carter: For the 48h bench we'll emulate those nightly spikes. We'll also include a 2x stress test to verify autoscale and queuing behavior.
[08:20] Lisa Park: For concurrency, our frontend opens websocket per user session — does Redwood support streaming and websocket connections?
[08:28] Alice Monroe: Yes, streaming support and function/tool calling are supported. We'll test with streaming enabled for the chat path.
[08:36] Rajesh Kumar: How do you measure cost for streaming vs non-streaming? We don't want hidden costs on many small messages.
[08:44] Ben Carter: Costs are token-based; streaming doesn't change token billing, but it changes latency characteristics and connection concurrency. We'll show per-route token cost in the POC reports.
[08:55] (discussion about batching, quantization specifics)
[09:02] Ben Carter: For embeddings we recommend quantized 16-bit or 8-bit depending on corp requirements; for chat smaller models in fp16 often give best latency. We'll test quantization configs in bench.
[09:18] Marco Diaz: One concern: if we quantize the 70B to save cost, how do we detect quality regressions?
[09:25] Ben Carter: We'll run your eval set and compute quality delta metrics (BLEU-ish and domain-specific checks plus manual spot checks). We'll flag any >X% drop for review.
[09:38] Rajesh Kumar: Timeline wise if we get the SOW by Thursday (12/24) and we kick off the bench week of 12/27, when could we expect results?
[09:47] Alice Monroe: 48h bench then 3 business days analysis — so early Jan first week for a full report.
[09:55] Lisa Park: For the POC environment credentials and networking, who will set that up?
[10:00] Ben Carter: We'll coordinate: Redwood SE will provide onboarding steps, you'll provision an allowlist or peering. Nina will help with firewall rules.
[10:10] Nina Chen: I'll need a diagram of network flows and egress IPs.
[10:14] Alice Monroe: We'll include that in the onboarding doc.
[10:20] (15 min left - go through sample traffic details)
[10:21] Marco Diaz: Quick sample stats we will provide: per-request token counts, timestamps, user/session id (hashed), request type tag (chat/embedding), and a small eval set of 200 support prompts.
[10:35] Ben Carter: Perfect. For the benchmark we'll align on scenarios: steady-state average, peak bursts, nightly embed batch, and 2x stress run. We'll capture cost and latency, and produce recommendations: model size, batching config, caching hints, and whether Dedicated is recommended.
[10:50] Rajesh Kumar: Criteria to move from POC to Dedicated: 1) meet chat P95 < 400ms at real traffic, 2) cost per 1M tokens under our threshold (TBD), 3) security checklist complete.
[11:05] Alice Monroe: We'll capture those as success criteria in the SOW. Anything else?
[11:12] Lisa Park: Please include a runbook for fallback behavior and a rollback plan if production rollout causes regressions.
[11:18] Ben Carter: We'll add that.
[11:25] (recap)
[11:27] Alice Monroe: Quick recap and next steps: Redwood to send SOW + security docs by 12/24; Skybridge to share 7-day anonymized traffic by 12/23; bench kickoff week of 12/27; SE to run 48h benchmark and deliver results first week of Jan.
[11:40] Rajesh Kumar: Sounds good, thanks.
[11:44] Alice Monroe: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in an email with links and the action items.

End of transcript
